Hope you had a good weekend. We’re coming up on our contract end (Sep 30) and have a couple of asks as we look to renew:

- We expect +40% peak capacity needs for Q4 (holiday traffic). Need a reliable burst buffer and predictable unit pricing.

- We’d like to discuss a credits/rebate structure tied to ops milestones (onboarding throughput, latency SLA).

Can you send over a proposal that includes: a short-term burst safeguard, a pricing ladder for committed usage, and an option for a progressive rebate if we meet staged adoption milestones?

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear summary. I put together a short proposal (attached) that aims to balance predictability for Lattice with capacity flexibility:

Highlights:
- Term: 12 months with an optional 6‑month extension.
- Commit bands: tiered discounts at 0–500k / 500k–1.2M / 1.2M+ token units.
- Price-hold: full price protection for the first 90 days after renewal, then standard tier pricing.
- Burst safeguard: a temporary burst credit pool (equivalent to 20% of committed units) usable during Q4 spikes; exhausted credits bill at a capped overage rate.
- Progressive rebate: up to 8% rebate distributed across three operational milestones (onboarding throughput, latency SLA, and adoption threshold). Rebate vests only after milestone verification by our CS team.

Open items for us to confirm with your team and finance:
1) Preferred invoicing cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
2) PO timing so we can lock capacity for Q4.
3) Which SLA metric matters most for the rebate verification (P95 latency, successful inference throughput, or error-rate)?

I attached a 1‑page proposal and a worksheet for modeling the rebate. Once Finance approves the economics, David can run final pricing approvals. Marissa — can you confirm we can present the proposed burst credit as a non-recurring onboarding concession (i.e., one-time credits) rather than a permanent rate change?

Attachment: LR_Renewal_Proposal_2027-07-21.pdf (proposal, 1 page)

Best,

Camila, David — quick internal notes before we mark this as ‘internal‑ok’:
- Burst credit: ok as a one-time Q4 safeguard. Cap total credits to 20% of committed units for the term; any additional spikes bill at the capped overage rate Camila proposed.
- Progressive rebate: finance prefers rebates be paid as credit against invoices, not cash refunds; limits the total rebate to 8% of ARR and ties vesting to documented milestones (CS signoff).
- Price‑hold: limited to first 90 days. For a 12‑month term we can extend the hold to 120 days if the customer signs within 10 business days of the proposal (incentive).
